summary.intent: Ship phase 70.1 of CipherBox (rotation-crash-resume-depth2 soundness work) as PR #598 through the /ship-phase flow, then verify all related todos were correctly retired to completed/.
summary.outcome: PR #598 achieved fully green CI (all cargo/Windows/macOS/Linux, Test, SDK-E2E, CodeRabbit, Greptile, Release Preview, Cross-Language Vector Parity, codecov) with 0 unresolved review threads; user then caught that the ship flow doesn't retire todos, so the assistant manually verified and moved the two resolves_phase:70.1 todos (rotation-crash-resume-depth2-soundness-gap, fuse-shared-scope-exit-rotation-live-wiring) to completed/ and pushed the commit.

repo: First-ever PR CI run on a long no-PR branch (96 commits) surfaced three pre-existing platform-gate failures that never ran before: SC#6 grep marker, Windows winfsp test_support cfg gate, and a Windows-incompatible permission-based floor_store test — these gates only trigger on PR CI, not local/branch work.

CodeRabbit caught a real TS/Rust twin-parity bug: the TS rotation engine GC'd a checkpoint before the parent republish committed, risking permanent subtree read-loss on crash; fix was porting the Rust engine's deferral logic to TS.
Todos use resolves_phase frontmatter to link to the phase that should close them; grep pending/ for resolves_phase to find retirement candidates.
workflow: The /ship-phase flow does not run todo retirement — that's execute-phase's job, and it can be skipped/incomplete, leaving resolves_phase-tagged todos stranded in pending/ even after the phase's work is fully merged and CI-green.

Before moving a todo to completed/, verify its full acceptance criteria (including embedded sub-findings like D-15a/b/c/d) are met, not just the headline fix — a todo can have caveats or separately-tracked limitations that stay open even when the main fix lands.
cargo fmt version-skew can be a trap in CI verification — this repo's CI doesn't fmt-check, so local fmt mismatches aren't blocking.

friction: Commit likely hung on 1Password signing at a timeout during the ship flow, requiring a manual check to confirm it actually landed.

Ship flow completion gave a false sense of full closure — the assistant had to be explicitly asked by the user whether todos were moved, revealing a gap in the automated flow (todo retirement wasn't run).
